name: Head of state
description: Top political leadership; motivated by national competitiveness and public visibility rather than technical delivery.

name: National government
description: Generic state actor, used when government is addressed broadly rather than a specific ministry.

name: Ministry of Education
description: The government body responsible for education-sector policy and school connectivity rollout.

name: Ministry of Health
description: The government body responsible for the health sector.

name: Ministry of ICT
description: The government body responsible for national ICT and telecom policy.

name: Youth/labour/social ministry
description: Government ministries responsible for youth employment, labour, or social development policy.

name: Telecom regulator
description: The arms-length regulatory authority responsible for spectrum, licensing and market rules.

name: Procurement officer
description: Government or school-system staff responsible for procurement and supplier compliance.

name: Government technical staff
description: Frontline or mid-level ministry and regulator staff who implement programmes day to day.

name: Finance minister / treasury
description: Finance ministry or treasury officials responsible for national budget allocation, fiscal policy and audit — a distinct compliance-driven path from sector ministries, focused on defensible evidence rather than programme delivery.

name: Development bank
description: Multilateral or bilateral financing institutions.

name: Development partner
description: Bilateral donors and implementing partners.

name: Multilateral / IGO
description: UN agencies and intergovernmental organisations (e.g. ITU, WHO) in coordination or standard-setting roles.

name: Telecom operator
description: National or regional network backbone operators.

name: Last-mile ISP
description: Small-scale or community-level providers serving the final connection.

name: Vendor
description: A contracted equipment or service supplier.

name: Local entrepreneur
description: Individual income-generating actors — innovators, farmers, gig workers — whose livelihood depends on connectivity.

name: NGO / civil society
description: Non-governmental and civil-society organisations.

name: Youth organisation
description: Organised youth-representative advocacy bodies.

name: Academia
description: Universities and research institutions.

name: Media
description: Press and media audiences.

name: School leader
description: An individual administrator or principal role.

name: Teacher
description: Instructional staff.

name: Health workforce
description: Clinical and health-facility staff.

name: Child
description: General child beneficiary, in a rights-based framing.

name: Student / learner
description: A child or person specifically in a learning context.

name: Youth / young person
description: Older adolescents and young adults, around workforce or civic engagement.

name: Woman / girl
description: Female beneficiaries, where gender-differentiated access gaps are the point.

name: Person with disability
description: Beneficiaries defined by disability status.

name: Household
description: The family or household unit as beneficiary.

name: Rural population
description: Beneficiaries defined by rural or remote geography.

name: Community
description: A local social grouping, not defined by geography alone.

name: Worker
description: Employed individuals, in a labour-market or productivity framing.

name: Firm / business
description: A business or company as the beneficiary unit.

name: Citizen / user
description: A generic individual user or citizen framing.

name: Unconnected person
description: An individual defined specifically by their connectivity status.

name: Patient
description: An individual receiving health care.

name: Mother / pregnant woman
description: Women in a pregnancy, childbirth or motherhood framing.

name: Infant / young child
description: Very young children, in a health-outcomes framing.

name: UNICEF country office
description: UNICEF country offices, who deliver Digital Inclusion work in-country and are an audience for internal alignment and capacity.
